security_audit.summary: All 80 static findings are false positives involving Markdown backticks, local project imports, entity identifiers, documented Goldsky URLs, or a placeholder webhook. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious execution in the reviewed source. Deployment and lifecycle commands remain operational actions requiring authorized projects, endpoint choices, and billing awareness.

content.value_statement: EVM applications need structured blockchain data through reliable GraphQL APIs. This skill guides Goldsky subgraph design, mapping development, testing, deployment, and endpoint configuration.
actual_capabilities: Guide instant subgraph deployment from contract ABIs or scaffold code-based projects with the Goldsky CLI.
Design GraphQL entities, scalar types, stable identifiers, immutable event logs, and derived relationships.
Author AssemblyScript mappings for ERC-20 transfers, ERC-721 ownership, and DEX factory templates.
Configure manifests, event handlers, contract calls, enrichment, and grafting.
Guide Matchstick testing and indexing optimization with declared calls, pruning, and lean schemas.
Configure GraphQL access, deployment tags, webhooks, and pause or start operations.
limitations: Subgraphs support EVM chains, not Solana, Sui, or other non-EVM networks.
Goldsky deployment requires installed CLI tooling, authentication, an authorized project, and paid infrastructure.
Native subgraph composition is unavailable; unified data requires separate endpoints or downstream pipelines.
Failure diagnosis and migration execution are delegated to related skills that must be available separately.

use_cases.title: Launch a token activity API
use_cases.description: Create an ABI-based GraphQL endpoint for contract events and assign a stable deployment tag.

use_cases.title: Model a protocol with custom entities
use_cases.description: Design token balances, NFT ownership, or pool relationships and implement tested AssemblyScript handlers.

use_cases.title: Reduce healthy indexing overhead
use_cases.description: Review contract calls, entity storage, pruning, and grafting constraints before planning an indexing optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an indexing approach
prompt_templates.prompt: I need GraphQL access to events from [contract] on [EVM chain]. Compare instant and code-based Goldsky subgraphs. Ask for missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: select a suitable subgraph workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an instant subgraph
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an instant Goldsky subgraph using [ABI file], [contract], and [chain]. Confirm the deployment block and project. Request approval before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Implement custom mappings
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ERC-20 tracker for [contract] on [chain]. Include entities, manifest, revert-safe mappings, and Matchstick edge-case tests. Do not deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: build and test custom indexing logic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a compatible optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [subgraph source] for excessive contract calls and storage overhead. Separate graft-compatible changes from schema changes. Preserve production and propose a verified cutover plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: optimize indexing without an unplanned production replacement.

output_examples.input: Plan a Goldsky GraphQL API for ERC-20 transfers without custom business logic.
output: Approach: instant subgraph from the contract ABI.
Required inputs: contract address, EVM chain, deployment block, ABI file, and target project.
Release plan: confirm project, approve deployment, assign a stable tag, and check indexing metadata.

output_examples.input: Recommend a schema for NFT ownership and transfer history.
output: Collection stores contract metadata and derives its token list.
Nft stores token identity and mutable ownership.
NftTransfer stores immutable transfer history with transaction-based identifiers.
Tests cover minting, transfers, and reverted metadata calls.

output_examples.input: Review a healthy DEX subgraph with slow historical indexing.
output: Prefer event payloads over repeated contract calls.
Declare independent calls and cache immutable metadata.
Use immutable swap logs and derived pool relationships.
Schema changes require a separate resync; preserve the original until replacement queries are verified.

best_practices: Confirm the GraphQL requirement, chain, contract deployment block, target project, and billing before deployment.
Regenerate types after schema changes and run mapping tests before publishing a new version.
Choose endpoint visibility deliberately and keep private API keys behind a backend.
anti_patterns: Deploying to the current CLI project without confirming authorization, billing, and production tag effects.
Replacing production with a lean schema before indexing and frontend compatibility are verified.
Storing growing parent arrays or making repeated contract calls when event data already provides the values.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It guides Goldsky subgraph creation for hosted GraphQL APIs over EVM contract data.

faq.question: Can I start without writing AssemblyScript?
faq.answer: Yes. Instant subgraphs use a contract ABI and configuration. Custom entity models or handler logic may require a code-based project.

faq.question: What must be available before deployment?
faq.answer: You need Goldsky CLI access, authentication, an authorized project, contract inputs, and a confirmed deployment plan. Each deployed version incurs charges.

faq.question: Does it support non-EVM or cross-chain subgraphs?
faq.answer: Subgraphs are EVM-only and index one chain each. Cross-chain workflows use separate endpoints or downstream data pipelines.

faq.question: Can it diagnose failures or migrate from The Graph?
faq.answer: Those workflows are delegated to subgraph-doctor and subgraph-migrate. This skill focuses on authoring, deployment, operations, and healthy indexing optimization.

faq.question: Are GraphQL endpoints private by default?
faq.answer: No. The reference states endpoints are public by default. Configure private access deliberately and keep API keys on your backend.
